findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot order audit logs by datetime
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does math.floor/ceil on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor integer. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page raises TypeError when building the next cursor, and any later page emits SQL comparing a timestamptz column to an integer (PostgreSQL error). DateTimePaginator already converts via strftime and fromtimestamp; this class does not, so optimized_pagination=true is unusable for the only endpoint that enables it.

findings.title: Negative-offset pagination raises on Django querysets
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and the client cursor offset is negative, get_result slices the queryset with a negative start (queryset[cursor.offset:stop]). Django QuerySet explicitly rejects negative indexes with ValueError, so the "advanced" path 500s instead of paginating. The same unclamped offset is also used for previous-page cursors in BasePaginator.get_result, so a crafted prev cursor can 500 any endpoint using that base class. Cursors are client-supplied via Cursor.from_string, which accepts a negative offset integer.

findings.title: In-place SET to ZSET change breaks existing span-buffer keys
findings.body: Span segment keys (span-buf:s:...) change from Redis sets (SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN) to sorted sets (ZADD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN/ZPOPMIN) without a new key prefix or migration. Keys written before deploy remain SETs until redis_ttl (default 3600s). Any Z* command against those keys returns WRONGTYPE, so process_spans and flush_segments fail for in-flight segments and those spans are dropped or stuck until TTL. A rolling deploy cannot safely mix old and new consumers on the same keys.

findings.title: Segments over 1000 spans are silently truncated
findings.body: After merge, the script ZPOPMINs span_count-1000 members (lowest end_timestamp_precise) with no metric or log. The flush path used to skip an oversized segment, increment spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded, and log; that check was removed from SpansBuffer._load_segment_data. Truncated segments are still flushed and produced as if complete, so spans are lost with no signal, and the cap is hardcoded at 1000 rather than SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (1001). There is no test that a segment larger than the cap drops the oldest members and still flushes the rest.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and can evict the wrong spans
findings.body: zunionstore is called without AGGREGATE MIN/MAX, so Redis defaults to SUM. If the same payload is already in both keys (retry, or the Python ZADD and a previous buffer both holding it), the merged score becomes the sum of end timestamps. zpopmin then treats that span as newest or oldest incorrectly and can drop a different span than the oldest one. sunionstore did not have scores, so this is a new failure mode of the set-to-zset conversion.

findings.title: Redirect walk cap cut from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops (previously 10000, with a comment that deeper segment trees would not join). When the cap is hit, the span is attached to an intermediate set_span_id instead of the true segment root. Deep traces are flushed as multiple incomplete segments, and the warning comment that documented this limit was removed. No test covers a chain longer than the new cap.
